report.headline: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES met its primary endpoint with a 15% relative risk reduction in MACE (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.78–0.93, p=0.0003) and showed a consistent all-cause mortality benefit (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73–0.98).
report.summary: In 18,924 post-ACS patients on maximally tolerated statins, alirocumab reduced the composite of coronary death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or unstable angina hospitalization over a median 2.8-year follow-up. The observed HR 0.85 closely matches the mechanism-predicted HR 0.798 derived from a 62% LDL-C reduction. Genetic evidence strongly supports PCSK9 as a causal target (Open Targets association score 0.949; loss-of-function variants associate with 15–28% lower LDL-C and CHD HR 0.79–0.81). Safety was favorable: injection-site reactions increased (3.8% vs 2.1%), but neurocognitive events (1.5% vs 1.8%) and new-onset diabetes (9.6% vs 10.1%) were similar. The trial constitutes a robust success; the calculator’s ‘insufficient_data’ prediction stemmed solely from missing total MACE event count.
key_evidence: Primary MACE HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.78–0.93, p=0.0003) — Praluent (alirocumab) significantly reduced risk of cardiovascular events in high-risk patients, and was associated with lower death rate (Sanofi/Regeneron, filed as SEC Form 6-K Ex. 99.2)
All-cause mortality HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.73–0.98, p=0.026) — same source
Subgroup with baseline LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL: HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.65–0.87) — same source
LDL-C reduction 62% (mechanism-predicted HR 0.798) — same source and calculator

PCSK9 genetic association score 0.949; loss-of-function variants: ~15–28% LDL-C reduction, CHD HR 0.79–0.81 — opentargets:PCSK9 and Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease
Safety: injection-site reactions 3.8% vs 2.1%; neurocognitive events 1.5% vs 1.8%; new-onset diabetes 9.6% vs 10.1% — Praluent announcement
report.what_would_change_this: Publication of the full manuscript with exact MACE event counts and Kaplan-Meier curves would confirm the event-driven power and allow precise calculator validation.
report.readthrough_note: Consistent with FOURIER (evolocumab) which showed similar MACE reduction (HR 0.85) and mortality trend; both PCSK9 inhibitors validate the target. Ongoing trials in primary prevention (e.g., NCT03705234) will extend evidence.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: PCSK9 genetic association score 0.949 for coronary artery disorder (Open Targets, f_8497e010f1677d), exceeding the 0.5 threshold. Pre-cut-off literature confirms the direction: PCSK9 nonsense mutations associated with 28% LDL-C reduction and protective effect on coronary heart disease (f_1ae580996b2635, pmid:16554528, 2006-03-01), and PCSK9 sequence variation associated with 15% LDL-C reduction and HR 0.79 for coronary heart disease (f_de6b1283c29bf7, pmid:16554528, 2006-03-01). Score >= 0.5 with coronary-disease studies -> causal.
missing: total primary endpoint (MACE) events count for ODYSSEY OUTCOMES
mechanism.notes: LDL-C change of -62.0% is placebo-adjusted, phase 3, from the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES announcement (2018-03-10), dose 75 mg and 150 mg Q2W (f_cd8c98d557978c). This is the outcome trial's own biomarker effect (preference a). No ODYSSEY OUTCOMES-specific baseline LDL-C is in the verified facts; pooled analysis baselines are 126.8 mg/dL (f_d4dae8f60afdf7) and 123.2 mg/dL (f_1c865f7a68f3ef) but are not outcome-trial-specific. Total MACE events count is not in the verified facts despite the trial having read out. ApoB changes for ODYSSEY OUTCOMES are only available from phase 1 (10 weeks), not preferred over the phase 3 LDL-C result.

issues.issue: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES-specific baseline LDL-C not in verified facts. Calculator assumed 2.0 mmol/L (77 mg/dL) to compute ldl_equivalent_mmol=1.24 from -62% reduction.
